brief: Morgan Stanley quantifies 2027 AI capex at $1.6 trillion, including $195bn of previously invisible lease-financed spending, and maps it to $1.7 trillion of supplier revenue. AI capex drives about 25% of S&P 500 sales growth, and a 42-name "Core to Thesis" cohort drives 78% of 2027 earnings growth while holding only 37% of index net income, so a capex slowdown becomes an earnings shock with no offsetting business. Within that total, Nvidia alone absorbs 67% of the S&P's capex-linked revenue, about $690bn or 44% of the whole budget; stripped of Nvidia, AI capex is worth just 1.6% of index sales. MS flags that private-stake markups inflated 2026 AI-cohort earnings, a risk made concrete this week when Anthropic's IPO investors cut its valuation to $1.5 trillion. The buildout is increasingly debt-funded: $1.1 trillion of signed-not-started leases, $255bn of bonds issued year-to-date, and MS modeling Oracle and SpaceX's combined interest coverage collapsing to 1.8x on new issuance, consistent with CoreWeave's implosion and Goldman's "phase two" unwind. MS also models a 32GW US power shortfall through 2028, widening further after. MS itself leans toward capex easing because returns stay strong; the author argues capital availability, not compute demand, is the binding constraint.
